headline: Jack Clark, co-founder of the AI company Anthropic, renewed his call for strong laws on advanced AI, saying today's lack of rules is like a race car with no brakes.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a lab co-founder repeats a known position at an international forum; it adds no new policy.
importance_line: A leader of a top AI lab asking governments for binding rules matters to the public and to lawmakers deciding how to oversee advanced AI, but Anthropic is a company with its own interests and Clark's reading of the US and Chinese positions is his own.
summary: Asharq Al-Awsat reports, citing AFP, that Jack Clark, co-founder of the AI company Anthropic and its head of public benefit, told an event at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday that the toys he buys for his children are "regulated more than the literal super intelligence I work on", and compared the industry to a Formula One car "at night without maybe brakes". Clark said the Trump administration, which wants the industry to police itself, is against regulation while China is not, and the report adds that Anthropic's idea of international coordination to slow the whole industry has so far not happened.
notes: The pool link (The Economic Times) held no readable text, so the story was read at Asharq Al-Awsat, which cites AFP; the url is the page where the text was read. Reuters (via Financial Express) also carries Clark's 'common sense standards' remark from the same panel. Overlaps with C05-02.
